answer: At a coastal haven, agents map how a rising tide changes a salt meadow. Each paid task names a random survey plot and a brief collection window; its signed sensor readings are checked against independent reference stations. The market merges matching plot records before paying, so twenty identities resending one observation earn only once. To collect more, a Sybil operator must place calibrated devices at different plots and lock a bond that false readings can forfeit. Location spoofing or colluding station operators remain possible, so surprise field audits are still needed.
